expect: Mastering (10-12): Both sides developed with named sources; justified conclusion. Arguments in support: Amrit Sanskar (Rahit Maryada 11-13) is the moment of formal entry into the Khalsa — it is the decisive commitment to the full Sikh code of conduct; the Five Ks are visible markers of Sikh identity and faith; Vaisakhi (when many take Amrit Sanskar) commemorates the founding of the Khalsa itself; wearing the Kirpan is a commitment to defending truth at personal risk. Arguments against: Naam Karan links the child's identity to the Guru Granth Sahib from birth — it is the ceremony that begins Sikh life; the Akhand Path (Rahit Maryada Chapter 7) is performed at all major life events and may be seen as more universally important because it applies to both Khalsa and non-Khalsa Sikhs; many devout Sikhs who have not undergone Amrit Sanskar practise Nam Japna, sewa and attend the gurdwara faithfully — the non-Khalsa path is also valid. Secure (7-9): Both sides; Rahit Maryada Chapter 7 or 11-13 named. Developing (4-6): One-sided. Emerging (1-3): Brief.
